The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) replied, "Wa Alaykumus Salaam." When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) granted permission. As Hadhrat Umar (RA) pushed open the door, he found that it had no lock. The two men entered the dark room and Hadhrat Umar (RA) had to feel his way around until he found Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA). When Hadhrat Umar (RA) felt the pillow of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), he found that it was made from the blanket used on animals. When he felt the ground, there was only sand and when he felt the clothing of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), he discovered that it was a flimsy shawl.
Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) asked, "Who is this? Is it the Ameerul Mu'mineen?" When Hadhrat Umar (RA) confirmed that he was the Ameerul Mu'mineen, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "You are late. We had been waiting for you all year." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "May Allaah have mercy on you. Have I not granted you sufficient wealth? Have I not given you plenty?" Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "O Umar! Do you not remember a Hadith that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned to us?" "Which Hadith?" asked Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) replied, "(The Hadith in which Rasulullaah ﷺ said,) 'The limit of a person's possessions in this world should be like the provisions of a traveller.'" "Oh yes (I have heard the Hadith)" confirmed Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then asked, "Now what have we done after Rasulullaah ﷺ, O Umar?" The two Sahabah (RA) then continued reminding each other (of the words of Rasulullaah ﷺ) with tears in their eyes until morning arrived. [^1]
Enquiring about the Condition of the Citizens
The Incident of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abu Saalih Ghifaari narrates that there was an extremely old blind lady living on the outskirts of Madinah whom Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to regularly visit at night. He would go there to fetch water for her (from the well) and do other chores for her. However, whenever he got to her, he would find that someone else had beat him there and had already seen to her needs. He went to her many times only to find that he was not the first to get there. (One day) He sat in wait for the person (who always beat him) and found that the person was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) would tend to the old lady even though he was the Khalifah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "By my life! It could only be you!" [^2]
Ibn Asaakir and Yashkari, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.77).
